Smt. Puja Barma (Roy)

Vs.
 Sri Sabyasachi Barma
 Mr. Abhimanyu Banerjee
 Ms. Reshmi Kelem ...for the petitioner

This is an application under Section 24 of the Code
 of Civil Procedure seeking transfer of Matrimonial suit
 no. 86 of 2022 presently pending before the court of
 learned Additional District Judge, Chandannagar,
 Hooghly to the court of learned Additional District Judge,
 Alipurduar.
The petitioner contended that the petitioner was  married with the opposite party on 22.2.2016 according  to Hindu Rites and Customs.

The petitioner alleged that  she was driven out from her matrimonial home on  1.
7.2021 and since then she has taken shelter at Birpara, Alipurduar.

The petitioner being an unemployed lady, has initiated a proceeding under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is pending before the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Alipurduar and she has further initiated another criminal proceeding under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code against the opposite party and her in laws, which is also pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, 2nd court, Alipurduar, where the husband/opposite party would be required to attend.

sentences.text:
All of a sudden, the opposite party/husband has instituted aforesaid suit seeking dissolution of marriage which is now pending before the court of learned Additional District Judge,
Chandannagar, Hooghly.
The petitioner submits that she has no independent source of income and she is maintained by her aged parents as the opposite party has not paid a single penny towards her maintenance.
The court at Chandannagar situates at a distance of 700 kilometres from her place of residence and involves journey of at least 16 hours in one way.
The petitioner further submits that she has no relative nor has any sort of accommodation near Chandannagar.
The petitioner is also suffering from several heath problems and her health does not permit to make such tidious journey.
Furthermore, she has no financial capacity to bear the large amount of travelling expenses.
Accordingly, she has sought for aforesaid transfer.

The petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the transfer application upon the opposite party by speed post with acknowledgment due with an intimation that the matter will appear under the heading "Hearing of Section 24 application" on 22nd June, 2023 and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.

Since the petitioner has made out an arguable case, let all further proceedings being Matrimonial suit no. 86 of 2022 presently pending before the court of learned Additional District Judge,
Chandannagar, Hooghly be stayed for a period of ten weeks or until further order, whichever is earlier.
CAN 1 of 2023 is accordingly disposed of.

(Ajoy Kumar Mukherjee, J.)
